# Soham Bhar

::: {.role}
Physics · Data Analytics · National University of Singapore
:::

Undergraduate reading Physics with a second major in Data Analytics, at NUS College.
My work sits where numerical methods meet experimental physics: writing the simulation
or the analysis pipeline, then checking it against something measured.

This repository is the record of that work. Every project here ships the code, the data
it ran on, the figures it produced, and the written report.

::: {.hero-links}

## [1.0] Abstract {#10-abstract}

::: {.reveal}

Six laboratory experiments and three computational studies, drawn from the physics
sequence at NUS. The emphasis throughout is on doing the numerical work by hand before
reaching for a library, and on carrying uncertainty all the way through to the quoted
result rather than stopping at a central value.

Two things distinguish this collection from a folder of submitted coursework. First, the
raw data is included: spreadsheets, instrument exports, simulation input decks. Second,
the analysis that turned that data into each figure is included as well. A reader who
doubts a number can follow it back to the measurement.

::: {.spec}

## [2.0] Applied engineering {#20-applied-engineering}

::: {.reveal}

Tools used in the work below, rather than a list of everything encountered.

[Python]{.tag} [NumPy]{.tag} [SciPy]{.tag} [Matplotlib]{.tag} [Jupyter]{.tag}
[MATLAB]{.tag} [R]{.tag} [Typst]{.tag} [LaTeX]{.tag} [Quarto]{.tag} [Git]{.tag}
[SRIM / TRIM]{.tag} [Excel]{.tag}

**Numerical methods.** Fourth-order Runge-Kutta written from scratch, LU decomposition
of a configuration-dependent mass matrix, eigenbasis decomposition against Airy
functions, Monte-Carlo binary collision simulation, Poincaré sectioning, bifurcation
mapping and Lyapunov divergence.

**Experimental methods.** Resonance spectroscopy, beam profiling, Hall measurement across
carrier types and temperature, Bragg diffraction, torsion dynamometry, and error budgets
propagated to the quoted figure.

:::


## [3.0] Selected work {#30-selected-work}

::: {.reveal}

::: {.entry}
### [Driven Quadruple Pendulum](projects/quadruple-pendulum/index.qmd)
::: {.meta}
[3.1] PC3236 Computational Methods in Physics · Python, Jupyter, Typst
:::
Four coupled masses with no closed-form solution, integrated with a hand-coded RK4 scheme
at a fixed 1 ms step rather than a library solver, so the integration behaviour stays
open to inspection. The 4x4 mass matrix is solved by LU decomposition at every stage.
Validated against SciPy's adaptive RK45 and agreeing to within one microradian over a
20 s trajectory, then characterised through Poincaré sections, bifurcation diagrams and
Lyapunov divergence.
:::

::: {.entry}
### [Quantum Bouncer](projects/quantum-bouncer/index.qmd)
::: {.meta}
[3.2] PC2130 Quantum Mechanics 1 · Python
:::
A particle in a linear gravitational potential above a hard floor, one of the few systems
with an exact solution in Airy functions. Energy eigenvalues taken from the zeros of the
Airy function, a Gaussian packet decomposed onto that eigenbasis, and time evolution by
resumming phase factors, so the propagation is exact rather than a finite-difference
approximation. The packet spreads, decoheres into an interference pattern with no
classical analogue, and later reassembles as a quantum revival.
:::

::: {.entry}
### [Interaction of Ions with Matter](projects/experimental-physics/index.qmd)
::: {.meta}
[3.3] PC3193 Experimental Physics II · SRIM, Python
:::
Twenty-five Monte-Carlo binary collision simulations of ion implantation, covering
hydrogen, boron, argon and gold into beryllium, silicon and gallium arsenide across six
orders of magnitude in energy. Ion ranges, damage profiles and sputtering yields extracted
by scripted analysis. Every `TRIM.IN` input deck is published, so any figure in the report
can be regenerated from scratch.
:::

:::


## [4.0] Laboratory record {#40-laboratory-record}

::: {.reveal}

Five bench experiments from PC2193, each published with its raw data and the workbooks the
analysis was carried out in.

| Ref | Experiment | Measured quantity |
|---|---|---|
| [4.1] | [Electron Spin Resonance](projects/experimental-physics/index.qmd) | g-factor of a free radical by resonant microwave absorption |
| [4.2] | [Gaussian Beam Optics](projects/experimental-physics/index.qmd) | Beam waist, Rayleigh range and beam quality factor |
| [4.3] | [Hall Effect in Germanium](projects/experimental-physics/index.qmd) | Carrier concentration and mobility, n-type and p-type |
| [4.4] | [X-Ray Diffraction](projects/experimental-physics/index.qmd) | Lattice constants of LiF and KBr, and Planck's constant |
| [4.5] | [Magnetic Moments](projects/experimental-physics/index.qmd) | Torque in a Helmholtz field against five variables |

:::


## [5.0] Reproducibility {#50-reproducibility}

::: {.reveal}

Fourteen CSV runs sit behind the Hall effect report, including zero-field and zero-current
controls. Four workbooks sit behind the X-ray diffraction analysis. Forty simulation input
decks sit behind the SRIM study. The bulk per-ion collision dumps are not published, since
SRIM regenerates them from the decks, but everything needed to do so is here.

Where the analysis was carried out in Excel, the workbook is published with its plots and
fitting intact rather than reduced to a table of results.

:::
